scheme_name: Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana
description:
The Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana is a welfare scheme launched by the Government of India to support construction workers in their pursuit of sports excellence. 

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2021. 

The primary objective of this initiative is to promote sports among construction workers and their children. 

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to talented individuals who are engaged in construction work. 

It seeks to identify and nurture sports talent among the children of construction workers. 

The government has set a measurable target of identifying at least 10,000 talented athletes from the construction worker community within the first two years of the scheme. 

The benefits under this scheme include financial support for training, equipment, and participation in national and international competitions. 

Eligible beneficiaries can receive up to ₹5 lakh for training expenses. 

Additionally, the scheme provides a one-time grant of ₹1 lakh for purchasing sports equipment. 

The financial assistance is intended to cover expenses related to coaching, travel, and competition fees. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme are clearly defined. 

Beneficiaries must be children of registered construction workers. 

The age limit for applicants is set between 6 to 25 years. 

The construction worker must be registered under the Building and Other Construction Workers Act, 1996. 

Income criteria stipulate that the family income of the construction worker should not exceed ₹15,000 per month. 

Educational qualifications are not strictly required for participation in the scheme. 

The application process for the Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must fill out the application form available on the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

The application form requires details such as the applicant's name, age, and the name of the construction worker parent. 

Applicants must also provide proof of the parent's registration as a construction worker. 

Documents required for application include a copy of the parent's registration certificate, proof of income, and age proof of the applicant. 

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the local Labour Department office. 

The timeline for processing applications is typically within 30 days from the date of submission. 

Disbursement of funds is scheduled to occur within 15 days after the application is approved. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

The Labour Department at the state level is responsible for the execution and monitoring of the scheme. 

Contact details for inquiries can be found on the Ministry of Labour and Employment's official website. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sports as a means of improving physical health and mental well-being among construction workers and their families. 

The initiative is part of a broader effort by the Indian government to promote sports and physical fitness across various demographics. 

The government recognizes the potential of sports as a career option and aims to provide the necessary support to underprivileged sections of society. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme encourages local sports clubs and associations to engage with beneficiaries. 

This engagement is intended to provide additional training and exposure to competitive sports. 

The scheme is expected to foster a sense of community among construction workers and their families. 

It aims to create role models within the community who can inspire others to pursue sports. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years. 

This budget is intended to cover training, equipment, and other related expenses for the beneficiaries. 

The scheme also includes provisions for organizing local and regional sports events to encourage participation. 

These events will serve as platforms for identifying talent and providing exposure to competitive environments. 

The Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana is a significant step towards inclusivity in sports. 

It aims to break down barriers faced by economically disadvantaged groups in accessing sports opportunities. 

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of this scheme reach the intended beneficiaries effectively. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation mechanisms are in place to assess the impact of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries will be collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of "Khelo India" which aims to promote sports at the grassroots level. 

It is also part of the larger framework of welfare schemes aimed at improving the livelihoods of construction workers. 

The initiative is expected to contribute to the overall development of sports culture in India. 

By supporting construction workers and their children, the scheme aims to uplift an often-overlooked section of society. 

The government encourages all eligible construction workers to take advantage of this scheme. 

Awareness campaigns are being conducted to inform potential beneficiaries about the available benefits. 

The Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana represents a commitment to fostering talent and promoting sports among the underprivileged. 

It is a crucial step towards ensuring that every child, regardless of their background, has the opportunity to excel in sports. 

The scheme is expected to create a positive ripple effect in communities, promoting health, fitness, and teamwork. 

Overall, the Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana is a comprehensive initiative aimed at empowering construction workers and their families through sports. 

It provides a structured approach to talent identification and support, ensuring that financial barriers do not hinder potential athletes. 

The initiative is a testament to the government's commitment to social welfare and sports development in India.
